venue.name: Greater Victoria Public Library
venue.description: Greater Victoria Public Library has been part of the community since 1966 and runs 12 branches serving over 350,000 residents across the region. Each branch has a children's area designed for play, reading and imagination, and some hold TechPlay STEM toys and Yoto players. The library offers space and support for teachers and early childhood educators to bring groups in for learning visits, and teachers can apply for student library cards ahead of a class visit using a Pre K-8 form. Free storytime sessions for younger children and their families run at several branches.

facility_notes.washrooms: All GVPL branches, including ours, have wheelchair-accessible entrances, washrooms, and computers.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The Central Branch has an elevator to access the second floor. We welcome service animals.

venue.hours_notes: Central Branch: Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 10:00 am to 6:00 pm; Tuesday and Thursday 10:00 am to 7:00 pm; closed Sunday. Hours differ at each of the 12 branches.

programs.name: Class visit to the library
programs.description: GVPL offers space and support for teachers and early childhood educators to bring groups to a branch for learning visits. Teachers can apply for student library cards ahead of the visit using a class visit form; the form is headed "Library Card Application Form for Pre K-8 Students" and is dated August 2025, and it asks a parent or guardian to consent and take responsibility for the card. The site directs groups to Contact us for help organizing a classroom visit. Schools, daycares, nonprofits and other organizations in the GVPL service area can also apply in person for a corporate library card. Visit length, group size, notice required and which branches host visits are not published.
programs.what_children_do: Arrive at the branch with the class, spend time in the children's area, and pick books to borrow on their own card if a parent signed the form beforehand.
programs.our_note: Nothing about the shape of the visit is on the site, so treat it as a conversation with one branch rather than a program you book off a page. Send the card forms home early; each needs a parent signature before the day, and a child without one cannot take a book home.
programs.practical_summary: Every branch has wheelchair-accessible entrances, washrooms and computers, and Central has an elevator to the second floor. Group size, visit length, lead time and somewhere to eat lunch are not stated anywhere on the site.
programs.evidence: Teachers bringing students to the library can apply for library cards ahead of time using a class visit form.

programs.name: Family Storytime with Stay & Play
programs.description: Stories, songs, rhymes and puppets for younger children and their families, followed by 30 minutes of social time and free play. Children must be accompanied by an adult. The sessions listed for mid-September 2026 run 10:30 to 11:30 am at the Central, Saanich Centennial, Oak Bay and Juan de Fuca branches. The page does not state an age range, a capacity, or whether registration is needed, and the programme runs in seasonal sessions rather than continuously.
programs.what_children_do: Sit with an adult for stories, songs, rhymes and puppets, then spend half an hour playing and mixing with other families in the branch.
programs.our_note: This is a public session, not a booked group slot, so a daycare group would be joining whoever turns up that morning. Ask the branch first whether a group of ten is welcome. Every child needs an adult with them, which fixes your ratio at one to one.
programs.practical_summary: Free, indoors, an hour long, at branches with wheelchair-accessible entrances and washrooms. Age range, capacity and whether you need to register are not published, and the session list changes each season.
programs.evidence: enjoy fun-filled stories, songs, rhymes, and puppets, followed by 30 minutes of social time and free play. Children must be accompanied by an adult.
